title: Developer Panic Mode: Streaming Fallbacks & Tool-call UX (PRD, WIP)
summary: Sketch for a new "panic mode" developer-configurable behaviour for hosted streaming calls that prioritizes availability and low tail-latency by enabling aggressive fallback strategies (model variant fallback, truncated structured outputs, synchronous tool call hedging) and SDK ergonomics to make the tradeoffs explicit and safe.
problem_statement: Some customers build interactive experiences that must never block for more than X ms. When backend model latency or downstream tool outages occur, apps either stall, return poor UX, or implement brittle client-side hacks. We need a standard server-side offering and SDK primitives that let developers opt-in to a predictable, observable set of fallback behaviors at the call level so apps remain responsive while preserving data safety and developer control.
goals: Provide a configurable, single-call flag (panic_mode) that activates a curated fallback policy for streaming endpoints
Define deterministic server-side fallback steps: model-variant fallback, partial-structured-output commit, tool-call hedging, and graceful truncation with developer-visible signals
Expose SDK patterns that make it easy to detect, test, and debug panic-mode behavior without leaking complexity into app code
Ship telemetry and SLOs that measure effectiveness (reduction in blocking time) and cost/regression signals (quality deltas, tool retry counts).
non_goals: Automatic application-level intent rewriting (we will not modify user prompts to circumvent failures)
Replacing long-term reliability engineering of tool integrations; panic mode is an availability band-aid, not a permanent fix
Complex interactive UI libraries — we provide primitives, not UI components
success_metrics: Reduce median and 95th percentile streaming stall time for panic_mode calls by >60% in field experiments
<= 5% increase in per-token cost for panic_mode traffic compared to baseline (target depends on hedging config)
<2% customer opt-out rate after first 90 days (indicates acceptable output quality tradeoff)
Telemetry spikes (tool retries, fallback counts) are surfaced within the Console within 5 minutes
user_personas: Primary persona: product/ML engineer building interactive features (chat, assistant, IDE integrations) that require tight latency ceilings; secondary persona: platform engineer who wants predictable behavior across tenants.
user_stories: As an engineer, I want a single API flag to opt-in to aggressive fallbacks so I can keep my UI responsive under transient outages
As an SRE, I want telemetry showing how often panic-mode assigned fallbacks are used so I can triage flaky tools
As an SDK consumer, I want callback hooks that let me display explicit UI states (e.g., partial_result, degraded_tool_response) so the product can inform users
proposed_api_surface:
Add top-level request parameter: panic_mode: {enabled: boolean, strategy: string, max_degradation: number, prefer_partial_output: boolean}. Example (pseudocode):

POST /v1/streams/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-xt-3b",
  "prompt": "Explain TLS handshake...",
  "panic_mode": {
    "enabled": true,
    "strategy": "latency-first", 
    "max_degradation": 0.25,
    "prefer_partial_output": true
  }
}

Behavior notes: server interprets strategy and runs fallbacks in order until content is ready or budget exhausted. SDKs expose a typed event stream: on_partial_output, on_fallback_engaged, on_tool_hedge, on_final_commit. The response includes metadata fields (fallback_trace, quality_estimate) appended to final event.

Security/contract: panic_mode cannot silence tool safety checks; tools that fail safety return safe placeholders and increment telemetry counters.
streaming_behavioral_spec:
Order of fallback operations (latency-first profile):
1) If primary model hasn't generated a token within tail_threshold_ms, spawn model-variant (smaller quantized) warmup and send partial tokens from the best available cache.
2) If tool call is blocking, issue a hedged call (concurrent 2nd call to secondary tool endpoint or simulated response) with a short timeout.
3) If structured output cannot be fully validated within validation_budget_ms, emit a 'partial_struct' event that contains the validated subset and a schema marker 'partial: true'.
4) If total budget hits max_latency_budget, abort remaining steps and emit best-effort summary with 'degraded: true'.

Each event contains: sequence_id, token_fragment (if present), fallback_trace (list of final-step labels), quality_estimate (0-1 string), and optional tool_trace ids. Clients must treat partial_struct as authoritative for displayed fields but not for downstream persistence unless they opt-in.

Developer note: these timelines are tunable per-call or via tenant policy. Default tail_threshold_ms = 800ms, validation_budget_ms = 200ms, max_latency_budget = 1500ms.
tool_calling_contract:
Tool calls initiated from panic_mode follow these rules:
- Tools are called with 'hedge=true' which means the platform may issue duplicate/parallel calls to alternative endpoints or cached simulators. Hedging is charged like two calls.
- Tools must implement idempotency tokens so duplicate calls are safe. If the integration cannot guarantee idempotency, tenants may disable hedging for that tool.
- Tool responses include status meta: {status: 'ok'|'degraded'|'failed', provenance: 'live'|'cache'|'simulated', latency_ms}.
- If both primary and hedged calls return 'degraded', panic_mode emits fallback_notice and optionally replaces tool output with a developer-provided fallback template.

Edge-case: synchronous blocking DB access called inside tool must be avoided; recommend async tool gateways with explicit timeouts. Integrations doc link included in linked_artifacts.
sdk_ergonomics_guidelines:
SDKs (JS/py/Go) will present a unified streaming event API and helper transforms:
- on('partial') -> receives partial structured payload + pragmas
- on('fallback') -> receives fallback_trace and human_readable_reason
- on('tool_event') -> tool provenance/latency
- helper: peekFinal({commitPolicy: 'auto'|'explicit'}) that either auto-commits partials into final result or requires explicit commit call from app.

Ergonomic principles: good defaults (no panic_mode), explicit opt-in, minimal callback surface (4 events), clear mapping to UI states, and local testing harness that can simulate fallbacks for dev-time QA. Provide code example and migration notes inside the SDK README.

Example UX pattern: show streaming cursor, first partial frames populate critical UI fields, and a non-blocking banner 'some fields are provisional'. When final commit arrives, banner auto-dismisses.
telemetry_and_slos:
Telemetry to emit per-call: panic_mode_enabled, fallback_steps (ordered list), final_quality_estimate, tool_hedge_count, model_variant_used, partial_commit_ratio, latency_ms (first_token, final_commit), cost_multiplier.

SLOs: panic_mode aims for 95th percentile time-to-first-visible-token <= 600ms by default. We will provide tenant-level policies to relax/generate different SLOs. Console alerts: when fallback rate > 2% of traffic for a route or quality_estimate drops below 0.6.

Alerting: playbook for ops includes prioritized alert types (tool degradation, hedging cost runaway, model fallback flapping). Telemetry must be available via Console and exported via metrics API (Prometheus-compatible).
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: enable panic_mode on a limited test tenant with SDK test harness; run synthetic failure scenarios (tool outage, model slow path). 2) Beta: invite 10 production customers on an opt-in basis; monitor quality deltas and cost. 3) Gradual GA: enable defaults off, feature flag rollout with tenant capability checks and automated cost guardrails. 4) Post-GA: iterate on strategy presets (latency-first, cost-aware, quality-first).\n\nTimeline: 3 month alpha --> 2 month beta --> 1 month GA prep. Console UX for telemetry must land before Beta. SDKs release in lockstep with server change.
open_questions: How do we compute quality_estimate reliably across model variants? (ML research input needed)
Should panic_mode be billable differently (e.g., hedged calls billed separately) or included as part of existing per-token pricing?
What legal/privacy constraints around simulated tool responses in regulated tenants?
Default thresholds: are the tail_threshold_ms and validation_budget_ms above appropriate for mobile use-cases?
